options.text: a wooden door
a metal box
a window
a brick wall

items.explanation: A window is made of clear glass, so light passes through it. Wooden doors, metal boxes, and brick walls block light.

items.prompt: Which is the SAFE way to use sound?

options.text: shout right next to a baby's ear
turn the volume up very high
bang pots as loud as you can
use a quiet voice indoors

items.explanation: Loud sounds near ears can hurt them, so a quiet voice indoors keeps ears safe.

items.prompt: Which is the SAFE way to use light?

options.text: look away when a light is too bright
stare straight at a very bright light
shine a flashlight into a friend's eyes
point a lamp at your eyes up close

items.explanation: Staring at a bright light can hurt your eyes, so looking away keeps them safe. Pointing lights at eyes is never safe.

items.prompt: Which example shows how sound behaves?

options.text: a radio plays music
a window lets light through
a mirror reflects light
a lamp lights a dark room

items.explanation: The radio's speaker vibrates to make music, which is sound. Windows, mirrors, and lamps are about light.

items.prompt: Which example shows how light behaves?

options.text: a window lets light through
a radio plays music
a drum makes sound when struck
a whistle makes a high sound

items.explanation: Clear glass lets light pass through, so the room is bright. Radios, drums, and whistles make sound.
